sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Described from a single incomplete specimen; it has not been confirmed by later collecting. The C. improbus recorded from New Zealand by Brauer (1868) is in fact C. brouni, not this species; Desneux (1904) held the same view.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: According to Emerson's 1927 record of his examination of the type specimens on behalf of the Berlin Museum: two alates, with a general label "improbus Hagen + Van Diem. Schayer". (i) Pin no. 2742 (holotype), only the head and pronotum remaining, the rest destroyed by insects: pronotum length 1.19 mm, compound eye diameter 0.45 mm, ocellus 0.11 mm from the compound eye, head width 1.58 mm. (ii) Pin no. 4052, label "Austral. Daewel (spelling doubtful)": head width 1.68 mm, compound eye diameter 0.50 mm, ocelli in contact with each other, pronotum length 1.13 mm; Emerson considered this specimen almost certainly a different species from the holotype of this species.

note: Adapted from the English entry in Hill (1942); the original has no separate Winged adult / Soldier / Worker description sections for this entry, only a synonymy list (8 entries, from Hagen 1858 to Froggatt 1915) and a note on the type specimens. Everything recorded here rests on Emerson's measurements, so only measurements of the surviving parts of the type specimens can be given. If the convention of recording entries that have only a list and a note as mention is applied, this entry could be downgraded to mention; the decision rests with the lead. OCR problems: the first line of the genus name reads "Calotermes" while the text reads "C."; "Linn. Ent om." is Linn. Entom.; before "Desneux, Gen. Insectorum" the text reads "Calotermes improuus nagen", i.e. improbus Hagen; "Proggatt" is Froggatt; "Agric. G-az." is Agric. Gaz.; "Taanania" is Tasmania; in Emerson's quotation the decimal forms "diam. of eye: .45" and "L. of pronotum 1,13" are copied as they stand (.45 is 0.45). The type locality Tasmania agrees with the list. Synonymy and nomenclatural history are not translated into the morphology section.
